newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam inflation steady before Tet spending spree.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam inflation steady before Tet spending spree.

text.p: Consumer prices remained under control in Vietnam this month, with the year-on-year inflation rate edging down to 4.4 percent from 4.5 percent at the end of 1996, the General Statistics Office (GSO) said on Monday.
Analysts said the figures suggested that early spending ahead of the Tet lunar new year festival, which falls next month, had not yet triggered upward pressure on prices.
Heavy spending on consumer goods, mainly food, ahead of Tet normally brings a spike in prices.

The GSO's index, which rose 0.8 percent from December, was skewed higher by a recent government-decreed increase in the cost of oil products, including petrol. Fuel prices rose 3.2 percent in January and 25.2 percent from a year earlier.
However, the cost of construction materials was unchanged from December and down 3.9 percent on the year.

The price of building materials normally rises during the November-February dry season. However, analysts say there has been a slowdown in construction activity and a build-up of industry stocks such as cement.

Vietnam's inflation rate plummeted last year, thanks largely to the government's tight monetary policy and an austere fiscal stance. The annual rate 12 months ago was 9.8 percent and 17.4 percent in January 1995.
Analysts say prices may pick up this year, partly due to the government's policy of allowing the dong to depreciate gradually against foreign currencies.
The depreciation drive is part of a plan to narrow the country's trade gap, which hit a record $4.0 billion last year.
